name: Switzerland (federal + canton and City of Zürich)
kernel_gaps: DBG Art. 36 is a printed cumulative table (amount per row + increment per complete 100 francs), rounded to 5 Rappen: written locally as TRow/tariffRp; the kernel Schedule is the band sum (OECD) and differs by up to 7 Rappen
federal tariff not progressive (13.2 % then 11.5 % of the whole income): Schedule.ticks_convex and splitting_le_separate do not apply (fedSingle_not_convex)
two tariffs chosen by household type (married / single parent use the Verheiratetentarif) rather than splitting: local
all-or-nothing deduction increase conditioned on other deductions being zero (DBG Art. 33 Abs. 1bis): local
family allowances with two entitlement routes (employee minimum income vs non-employed income test): local famzgEntitled
capital benefits taxed separately at a fraction of the tariff (1/5 federal, rate of 1/20 with a 2 % floor in Zürich): local
Out writes whole units: taxes kept in Rappen in detail (fedTaxRp, cantonTaxRp, ...)

headline: Reproduces the ESTV calculator on 1,494 of 1,494 lines and the OECD on 55 of 56; one franc paid into Säule 3a costs a saver without a pension fund 236 francs of tax (couple 498), the BVG threshold is a +84.63 notch, a 7,560 wage unlocks 5,160 of family allowances for a family living on capital income, and two-earner couples pay up to 71 % (135 % with children) more federal tax married.
notes: Family decision: default output = federal (incomeTax) + Zürich Staatssteuer 98 % + City of Zürich 119 % + Personalsteuer 24/adult (localIncomeTax), church tax off; --canton-only = literal CONTRACT38 reading (no Gemeindesteuer, no Personalsteuer); --church reformed|catholic adds 10 %. OECD SLT = canton + City + Personalsteuer, no church. Employee social = AHV/IV/EO 5.3 % + ALV 1.1 % (NBU optional --nbu, BVG deducted for tax but not in employeeSocial, as the OECD). Web searches used: 3 of 3.
